name: Controlled-300
description: This release contains the research artifacts for “Trustworthy Evaluation Frameworks for AI-Assisted Painting Restoration,” a master’s thesis at the University of Applied Sciences Technikum Wien. The study develops and applies an evidence-based evaluation framework combining traditional image quality metrics with perceptual, colour, texture, boundary, structural, robustness, and generative-uncertainty evidence. The Controlled-300 study covers 300 paintings across five categories, with 3,425 registered cases and 2,620 eligible cases. Four methods: OpenCV Telea, LaMa, HINT, and Stable Diffusion, provide 10,480 matched primary candidates. The broader reporting collection contains 13,879 retained candidates. Additional investigations include 1,025 four-seed Stable Diffusion uncertainty groups, damage-size sensitivity, mask robustness, synthetic degradation, and separate diagnostic studies. SDXL is included as a bounded feasibility investigation, not as a fifth full-coverage method. Across 2,320 matched non-zero-damage cases, LaMa achieved the best mean masked MAE (14.83) and crop LPIPS (0.1292), while Telea achieved the best mean crop SSIM (0.8632). These complementary results motivate examining restoration quality through multiple forms of saved evidence. The archive brings together source code, notebooks, configurations, painting provenance, experimental outputs, candidate restorations, diagnostic maps, metric tables, reports, and supporting documentation.
